attribution.note: Marcus wrote this in his own Substack post. The Altman passage is quoted as the object of Marcus's claim about what Altman said.

semantics.note: The revision correctly keeps Altman's 'I bet' wording rather than turning it into necessity. The 'dramatic sign' remark is labelled as Marcus's commentary. The checkable parts are the 2022 ridicule and the recent architecture remark.

contract.note: Requiring both attributions is fair, and so is letting 'just' cover a recently published recording. Commentary is correctly excluded from grading.

evidence.note: Altman's own dated April 2022 post mocks a 'mediocre deep learning skeptic' but does not name Marcus. It is a primary record of the ridicule, but on its own it does not identify the target.
Independent commentary identifies Marcus as the target and links the post. This corroborates the ridicule part only. It says nothing about the architecture remark.

reviews.rationale: The ridicule part has plausible support: Altman's April 2022 post plus independent commentary naming Marcus. However, the packet has no authenticated transcript or recording of the architecture remark, and the contract requires both parts. Nothing contradicts either part, so the claim as a whole is unresolved.

attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his Substack post.

semantics.note: 'And it hasn't' is a retrospective observation that scaling had not produced AGI by the time of the post. The claim that it never will is correctly left out.

contract.note: Marcus named no AGI threshold. The contract's plain reading, broadly human-level and flexible competence across domains without perfection, is fair and ordinary. If no AGI existed, scaling did not produce it, so there is no need to separate out scaling's role for support.

evidence.note: ARC Prize's December 2025 assessment states AGI is 'not yet' here. It is an independent benchmark body, though its snapshot predates the cutoff by about three months.

The International AI Safety Report 2026 is a broad scientific synthesis. It finds capabilities are 'jagged', with failures in multi-step work and long-term planning. That fits a lack of broad human-level competence under the plain reading.

The university reports its own researchers arguing that current LLMs are AGI under a lower, tiered threshold. This is a contrary view, but it is not an independent finding of broad human-level competence, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's ordinary reading, independent sources (ARC Prize in December 2025, the safety report in February 2026) document substantial missing general capabilities shortly before March 16, 2026. The UC researchers' contrary argument uses a lower bar and is a disputed position, not independent proof that AGI existed. The claim is supported, with the caveat that the snapshots end before March.

attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words. The quoted January 2025 Altman line is the object of Marcus's claim.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both the claim that Altman did not say the architecture was found and the 'retrenchment' characterisation, along with the scope of 'in this talk'. Marcus's quotation slightly paraphrases Altman's actual wording but keeps its meaning.

contract.note: Reading 'retrenchment' as a material retreat in confidence about the route to AGI is ordinary and fair. Whether the result holds turns on that reading, and Marcus gave no threshold.

evidence.note: Altman's January 2025 Reflections post confirms the earlier statement of confidence and its date. It supports only that premise, not any later retreat.

Same-event reporting from TreeHacks (February 2026) records Altman's continued confidence that AGI is near. This weakens the case for a retreat, but confidence about timing is not the same as confidence that the route is already known.

reviews.rationale: The full talk was not recovered, so the claim that Altman did not say the architecture was found cannot be checked across the whole talk. The earlier statement is confirmed. Reporting from the same event shows continued AGI optimism, which cuts against retreat but does not clearly meet the contradiction condition. The evidence does not settle the claim.
